title: Schematicity descends to a stage of an affine algebraic-space limit
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space] and universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic spaces over $S$, with affine transition morphisms. Quasi-compact means that every open cover of the underlying point space has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests. The point topology is [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is finite (respectively integral, affine) when every base change by a scheme is represented by a finite (respectively integral, affine) scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Suppose an algebraic space $Z$ over $S$ and compatible $S$-morphisms $Z\to Z_i$ form a limit in algebraic spaces over $S$: for each algebraic space $W$ over $S$, $S$-morphisms $W\to Z$ correspond bijectively to compatible families of $S$-morphisms $W\to Z_i$. If $Z$ is represented by a scheme, then $Z_i$ is represented by a scheme for some $i\in I$.

proof.text: For every $i$, apply the atlas criterion in [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] to the quasi-compact point space $|Z_i|$. It gives a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme to $Z_i$. Thus $Z_i$ is quasi-compact in the chart convention of [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages]. Its quasi-separatedness is the assumed quasi-compactness of the absolute diagonal on scheme tests, exactly the diagonal convention of that node. The given affine morphisms are representable with affine scheme pullbacks, so they also have precisely that node's meaning of affine.

source.place: Tag 03E4 (lemma-quasi-compact-space), atlas criterion; definition-separated for the absolute diagonal convention

proof.text: Let $L$ be the limit of the fppf sheaves associated to $(Z_i)$. By [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages], $L$ is an algebraic space. For any algebraic space $W$ over $S$, a map $W\to L$ is a compatible family of maps $W\to Z_i$: limits of sheaves have their compatible sections pointwise, and a map into that limit is uniquely specified by its component natural transformations. Consequently $L$ is also a limit in algebraic spaces over $S$. The assumed universal property of $Z$ now gives maps $a:Z\to L$ and $b:L\to Z$ commuting with every projection. The maps $ba$ and $\mathrm{id}_Z$ have the same projections, so the uniqueness in the limit property of $Z$ gives $ba=\mathrm{id}_Z$. Similarly $ab=\mathrm{id}_L$. Hence $Z\cong L$ as algebraic spaces over $S$.

source.place: Tags 07SF (lemma-directed-inverse-system-has-limit) and 07SR (lemma-limit-is-scheme), Situation 084R (situation-descent); reuse of existing combined DAG statement

proof.text: The scheme representing $Z$, composed with $a$, also represents $L$, since $a$ is an isomorphism of the corresponding sheaves. Apply the schematic-stage clause of [lem-sfb-space-affine-limits-schematic-stages] to this sheaf limit. The index set is small, directed and nonempty by hypothesis; step 1 checked that every stage is quasi-compact and quasi-separated in the conventions required there; all transition maps are affine by hypothesis. That clause gives an $i\in I$ for which $Z_i$ is a scheme, as required. This reuses the existing stronger node, including its affine-stage assertion, rather than creating another copy of Tag 07SR.
